Independent PCRE2 captures, binary cache keys, binding scope, replacement growth, bounded matching and stream-error recovery.

Strict UTF-8 grouping, malformed-byte recovery, open-pipe delivery and descriptor ownership. Display widths depend on libc; help write errors and grapheme equivalence remain outside scope.
Bounded GNU 1.07 language corpus, scalar/array scope restoration and duplicate declaration rejection. Preserve explicit POSIX-option, read/newline/status and stack-bounded recursion differences.
Native GNU byte/count/header/NUL records plus exact-consumption and descriptor ownership. Signals, live input mutation and cross-libc behavior remain unqualified.
Native and forced no-REG_STARTEND C/C.UTF-8 byte/record/BRE paths with branch-local empty-backreference guards. Actual musl, collating locales and every regex extension remain unqualified.

Newline records and C-locale byte fields with dynamic duplicate groups and invocation-owned stdin buffers. Repeated failed output cannot leak old input into redirected calls. Full locale/CLI and asynchronous-signal conformance remain unqualified.

Authenticated IPv4 loopback membership with one seed and at most 32 peers. Temporary environment lifetimes, child ownership and cleanup are tested; off-host deployment and maximum-capacity performance remain unqualified.

Trusted local repository parsing and builtin-to-installer protocol with an isolated recording installer. Embedded NUL/control records fail without truncation; actual bashy.box installation remains unqualified.

Owned-child wait status and private external-delegate behavior, plus synthetic authentication boundary fixtures. Real authentication, policy enforcement, account changes and privilege transitions remain unqualified.

Fixed-buffer compression/decompression, bounded decoder windows and atomic named output publication. Native stream and fault oracles plus isolated static-root execution qualify software paths; no durability or concurrent hostile-path guarantee.
Absolute-priority parsing and continuation with owned process/group targets; all-user selectors are intercepted. Smoke mutation targets only a disposable child and cannot change the invoking shell.
Exact operand count, pid_t bounds and owned-child process-group contracts. No live host process groups are changed; cross-architecture pid_t qualification remains separate.

Mutation preflight opens all destinations before writes, retains descriptors for rollback and checks verbose child output before exec. Tests retain predecessor assertions and use intercepted setters/private files.

Strict IPC identifiers and independent private SysV resource lifecycle plus injected failures. Only owned resources are removed; attached shared-memory lifetime and broader kernel variants remain separate.
Validated creation and exact payload/lifecycle checks for owned SysV/POSIX IPC resources, with cleanup and same-shell recovery. No arbitrary existing resources are accessed.

Strict key identifiers and synthetic/private anonymous-session key lifecycle. Tests never fall back to inherited keyrings. Kernel quotas, concurrent mutation and cross-account authority remain unqualified.

Private seed-file validation, consume-before-credit ordering, atomic replacement and injected error recovery. Native tests save or load missing private files; entropy-credit and power-loss qualification remain isolated-VM prerequisites.

Parsing and shutdown syscall sequence checked only through a fail-closed boundary interceptor. No live reboot, shutdown, sync or scheduler mutation occurs; actual platform shutdown requires a disposable VM.
Parser, directory-open and freeze/thaw syscall boundary with closed fixtures. Actual freezable filesystem behavior and latency require a disposable capable VM.
Loop parser, attach rollback, read-only propagation and complete backing-path association through closed ioctl fixtures. Actual kernel loop behavior requires a disposable loop-capable VM.

Ext2 layout checked by independent decoders and filesystem tools using private regular images, including write faults and cleanup. Block devices, mounting, crash recovery and real storage behavior remain unqualified.

Strict proc-swaps snapshot parsing, escape decoding, deduplication and failure continuation. A closed interposer and seccomp guard prevent real swapoff; live reclaim and permission behavior remain VM prerequisites.

RTC conversion, adjustment files and syscall sequencing exercised with fully intercepted setters and private state. Standalone sanitizers qualify software only; actual RTC/system-clock effects require an isolated VM.
FITRIM range semantics and util-linux comparisons in a private namespace with intercepted ioctls. Actual discard support and latency remain hardware prerequisites.

Raw device-mapper ioctl ABI, payload validation, rollback ownership and open-failure cleanup against a closed private fixture. Real mapper devices, udev coordination and deployment behavior remain VM prerequisites.

Linux echo requests with complete payload/checksum validation, monotonic deadlines and same-shell recovery. Native owned loopback and injected raw-socket paths are distinct; no traceroute or external network qualification.

Owned socket cases and deterministic netlink/proc fixtures qualify formatting, UDP selection and atomic per-family fallback. Truncated/interrupted dumps fail safely; corrected per-family buffering has no new timing claim.
Private queue and local SMTP fixtures qualify response classes, same-shell recovery and SIGPIPE-safe socket writes. No live delivery, credential or TLS-deployment qualification.

RTSP/TCP interleaved H.264 framing, authenticated root-relative control paths and bounded allocation checked with private loopback fixtures. Cameras, decoders, UDP RTP, TLS and IPv6-literal authorities remain unqualified.

Private owned-service lifecycle, readiness, backpressure and log framing. Service output drains while readiness probes run. Live service configuration, privilege transitions and durability are unqualified.
Local and isolated rsh-shim push parity, including multi-source deletion against the complete source union. Pull, native/daemon protocol, special files, ACLs and xattrs remain unqualified.

Private Linux PTY metadata, bounded active-reader delivery, exact queue boundaries, history and owned-session cleanup. Nonreaders may be evicted; injected UID checks do not qualify real cross-account enforcement.

PCRE2 integration with record-end anchors, explicit UTF invalid-byte handling, match limits and persistent-shell recovery. Retain POSIX embedded-NUL/libc, non-UTF locale and accepted-but-no-color limitations.
Dispatcher command contracts, exact literal tac separators and nproc environment overrides. The bounded dispatcher surface is distinct from the unfinished standalone general-regex tac task.

comm.note: Selected-column GNU comparisons and write-failure contracts have a dedicated regression. The historical 2026-09-12 comm case measured 0.50 times the external runtime; current performance needs a new measurement.

sort.note: Write-failure handling and selected GNU comparisons have dedicated regressions. The historical 2026-09-12 sort-text case measured 0.91 times the external runtime; it is not an open confirmed performance defect.

crypto.note: Nonce and AAD rejection tests preserve the key. Worker timings are wrapper/workload-specific, with unchanged production source after the test correction.
crypto.next: Retain independent cryptography oracles and bounded API coverage; no broad cryptographic security or uniform speedup claim.

rev.note: Write-failure stop and GNU comparison are covered by tests/rev-check.sh.

col.note: Repeated redirected stdin is fixed; tests/col-check.sh matches GNU on three fresh redirections. Output is newline-terminated as util-linux does, including an unterminated final line, which is what the large text fixture has. File operands are a bash-os extension: util-linux col reads stdin only and rejects an operand, so that path has no reference.

split.note: Repeated redirected input has dedicated comparisons; private fixtures also cover piece contents, input aliases and output failures.

csplit.note: Repeated redirected stdin is fixed; tests/csplit-check.sh matches GNU piece files across three redirections.

tee.note: Closed-stdin and all-outputs-failed stop are covered by tests/tee-check.sh. Stock examples/loadables/tee.c is still the source.

tail.note: Repeated small-input redirections and write-error stop are covered by tests/tail-check.sh.

ar.note: Truncated headers, extract write errors and short member bodies are rejected; tests/ar-check.sh matches GNU 2.44 including /dev/full unlink and archive-link identity.

du.note: A failed size-report write now returns failure; tests/du-check.sh covers du -b file > /dev/full.

mv.note: Self-moves fail without changing bytes. Additional fixtures cover long paths, cross-filesystem moves, modes and injected close/metadata failures.

truncate.note: Size arithmetic overflow is rejected and existing bytes are preserved; tests/truncate-check.sh matches GNU.

cp.note: An unreadable source preserves an existing destination. Additional fixtures cover recursive bounds, aliases, metadata and close failures; selected GNU comparisons are mapped in the CSV.

zstd.note: Fixed-buffer compression/decompression, bounded decoder windows and atomic named output publication. Native stream and fault oracles plus isolated static-root execution qualify software paths; no durability or concurrent hostile-path guarantee.
zstd.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

hostid.note: Default is gethostid(3), matching hostid(1), including on this measured full binary. tests/hostid-check.sh covers override files and the machine-id fallback.

free.note: Measured against a pinned /proc via BASHOS_PROC_ROOT, self-timed: the live counters move between the reference call and the repeated batch, so a live ratio could only ever fail. tests/free-check.sh holds the GNU parity.

coreutils.note: Dispatcher command contracts, exact literal tac separators and nproc environment overrides. The bounded dispatcher surface is distinct from the unfinished standalone general-regex tac task.
coreutils.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

mktemp.note: The former -u create-then-unlink defect is fixed: name-only generation leaves the filesystem untouched. The regression also covers ordinary file and directory creation.

passwd.note: Empty passwd fields retain their column positions in list and lookup paths; dedicated fixtures cover empty and malformed records. The historical timing fixture remains unchanged.

vi.note: Last-line deletion and inclusive UTF-8 visual endpoints are corrected. Historical editing timings precede the UTF-8 correction and include external-process startup.
vi.next: Macros, named registers, text objects and additional motions remain deferred; no full vi conformance or current-code speed ratio is claimed.

dmesg.note: The former split-record loss is fixed. Fixture checks cover records crossing read boundaries and an unterminated final record; device fixtures also exercise input bounds.

fstrim.note: FITRIM range semantics and util-linux comparisons in a private namespace with intercepted ioctls. Actual discard support and latency remain hardware prerequisites.
fstrim.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

rsync.note: Local and isolated rsh-shim push parity, including multi-source deletion against the complete source union. Pull, native/daemon protocol, special files, ACLs and xattrs remain unqualified.
rsync.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

lsattr.note: The flag field is 14 columns where e2fsprogs prints 22 for the same file, so the two cannot be compared on exact bytes.

obj.note: The getline(stdin) loops now clearerr(stdin) at the builtin entry: without it a second in-process `--batch-check`, `--batch`, `hash --stdin-paths` or `tree` emitted nothing while still exiting 0, because a builtin does not fork and the stream keeps its EOF flag.

bsdgames.note: ROT13 and explicit Caesar shifts have exact byte and persistent-stream fixtures. Argument output errors and stale read-ahead after early game exits are fixed. Current seven-sample historical workload measures 5.729 ms builtin / 8.600 ms GNU tr (0.666x); the historical slowdown does not reproduce on the current build. Only regular-file throughput is measured; representative adapter contracts do not establish full upstream game parity. Historical timing data remains unchanged.
bsdgames.next: Qualify other game adapters and pipe/TTY throughput if required.

ts.note: Capture precedence takes the last matching pattern rather than the most specific: in span mode a JSON object key yields both string.special.key and string, and the renderer paints it with the later, less specific rule.

git.note: The recorded parity run covers 69 scenarios and 414 comparisons. Dedicated integrity and apply-path regressions cover malformed storage, preflight failures, complete long patch lines and nested rename strip levels; this is not full Git compatibility.

pkg.note: Index verification uses the same byte buffer that is published. Separate trust and package-publication fixtures cover signature lookup, trust-file failures and install rollback, including sanitizer checks.

vt.note: Dedicated edge fixtures cover drained response cloning, complete combining sequences in diff/scrollback output and bounded CSI numeric parsing.

buf.note: Dedicated edge fixtures cover reload cleanup and saving through an aliased retained filename.

expect.note: A continuous-output child cannot extend the whole-wait deadline; the regression uses a private PTY.

ptybroker.note: Private Linux PTY metadata, bounded active-reader delivery, exact queue boundaries, history and owned-session cleanup. Nonreaders may be evicted; injected UID checks do not qualify real cross-account enforcement.
ptybroker.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

bashlogger.note: Private AF_UNIX sender contract and validated 5000-message API workload measured on 2026-10-19. Timing includes shell loop and Python receiver; no external ratio or host daemon/persistence qualification.
bashlogger.next: Qualify additional logger CLI or daemon integration behavior when required; current API measurement is separate from the historical catalog timings.

blockdev.note: All advertised software ioctl paths have closed fixtures and fixed query/request batch measurements on 2026-10-19. Shim time includes shell/module/fixture overhead; no hardware latency or external speedup claim.
blockdev.next: Actual device geometry, privileges, driver errors, flush and partition reread effects still need device qualification.

bashsyslogd.note: Owned-daemon software contract and three fixed loopback/queue workloads measured on 2026-10-19. Timestamp/send shims are labeled; intentional UDP overflow and bounded-spool drops are counted. Allocation-failure preservation was corrected after timing. No external performance ratio.
bashsyslogd.next: Qualify deployment-specific transport and persistence requirements; UDP forwarding and the single-daemon spool remain best effort without acknowledgements or crash durability.

fifo.next: FIFO API contract qualified with native and sanitizer checks. Worker measurements are self-timed API wall costs for their recorded binary; no terminal performance or external ratio is claimed.

more.note: Forward pager software paths and checked key helper are qualified. Original historical throughput slowdown was not reproduced; separate worker large-pipe measurements include producer/sink and shell costs.
more.next: Backward scrolling, wrapped-row accounting, full POSIX conformance and physical terminals remain unqualified.

pcre.note: Bounded PCRE API paths are qualified; literal grep fastpath timings are distinct from general regex engine throughput.
pcre.next: Retain native Linux scope, explicit PCRE API semantics and per-workload regressions; no GNU grep/sed command equivalence or leak-free claim.

zstdcat.note: Fixed-buffer compression/decompression, bounded decoder windows and atomic named output publication. Native stream and fault oracles plus isolated static-root execution qualify software paths; no durability or concurrent hostile-path guarantee.
zstdcat.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

renice.note: Absolute-priority parsing and continuation with owned process/group targets; all-user selectors are intercepted. Smoke mutation targets only a disposable child and cannot change the invoking shell.
renice.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

setpgid.note: Exact operand count, pid_t bounds and owned-child process-group contracts. No live host process groups are changed; cross-architecture pid_t qualification remains separate.
setpgid.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

ipcctl.note: Strict IPC identifiers and independent private SysV resource lifecycle plus injected failures. Only owned resources are removed; attached shared-memory lifetime and broader kernel variants remain separate.
ipcctl.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

ipcmk.note: Validated creation and exact payload/lifecycle checks for owned SysV/POSIX IPC resources, with cleanup and same-shell recovery. No arbitrary existing resources are accessed.
ipcmk.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

keyctl.note: Strict key identifiers and synthetic/private anonymous-session key lifecycle. Tests never fall back to inherited keyrings. Kernel quotas, concurrent mutation and cross-account authority remain unqualified.
keyctl.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

rngseed.note: Private seed-file validation, consume-before-credit ordering, atomic replacement and injected error recovery. Native tests save or load missing private files; entropy-credit and power-loss qualification remain isolated-VM prerequisites.
rngseed.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

halt.note: Parsing and shutdown syscall sequence checked only through a fail-closed boundary interceptor. No live reboot, shutdown, sync or scheduler mutation occurs; actual platform shutdown requires a disposable VM.
halt.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

reboot.note: Parsing and shutdown syscall sequence checked only through a fail-closed boundary interceptor. No live reboot, shutdown, sync or scheduler mutation occurs; actual platform shutdown requires a disposable VM.
reboot.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

poweroff.note: Parsing and shutdown syscall sequence checked only through a fail-closed boundary interceptor. No live reboot, shutdown, sync or scheduler mutation occurs; actual platform shutdown requires a disposable VM.
poweroff.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

fsfreeze.note: Parser, directory-open and freeze/thaw syscall boundary with closed fixtures. Actual freezable filesystem behavior and latency require a disposable capable VM.
fsfreeze.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

losetup.note: Loop parser, attach rollback, read-only propagation and complete backing-path association through closed ioctl fixtures. Actual kernel loop behavior requires a disposable loop-capable VM.
losetup.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

mkfs.note: Ext2 layout checked by independent decoders and filesystem tools using private regular images, including write faults and cleanup. Block devices, mounting, crash recovery and real storage behavior remain unqualified.
mkfs.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

swapoff.note: Strict proc-swaps snapshot parsing, escape decoding, deduplication and failure continuation. A closed interposer and seccomp guard prevent real swapoff; live reclaim and permission behavior remain VM prerequisites.
swapoff.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

hwclock.note: RTC conversion, adjustment files and syscall sequencing exercised with fully intercepted setters and private state. Standalone sanitizers qualify software only; actual RTC/system-clock effects require an isolated VM.
hwclock.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

ping.note: Linux echo requests with complete payload/checksum validation, monotonic deadlines and same-shell recovery. Native owned loopback and injected raw-socket paths are distinct; no traceroute or external network qualification.
ping.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

netstat.note: Owned socket cases and deterministic netlink/proc fixtures qualify formatting, UDP selection and atomic per-family fallback. Truncated/interrupted dumps fail safely; corrected per-family buffering has no new timing claim.
netstat.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

ss.note: Owned socket cases and deterministic netlink/proc fixtures qualify formatting, UDP selection and atomic per-family fallback. Truncated/interrupted dumps fail safely; corrected per-family buffering has no new timing claim.
ss.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

sv.note: Private owned-service lifecycle, readiness, backpressure and log framing. Service output drains while readiness probes run. Live service configuration, privilege transitions and durability are unqualified.
sv.next: Historical measurements retain their original source provenance; corrected-code timing and broader platform or hardware qualification are not claimed.

validation.summary: At measurement time, the full catalog contained 279 entries: 248 had individual command timings and 31 did not. The batch used seven samples per case, pinned to one CPU under the shared benchmark lock. The measured binary includes repeated-input fixes for more, less, uuencode, xargs, obj and bsdgames, affinity-aware coreutils nproc, and col output termination. The full test harness was not rerun for that measurement batch.
